title: Ash-Sharh 94:4-6 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: Ash-Sharh, Ad-Duha 1 to 8 and applying the rules
source: Written for quran/y3 lesson 32 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Ash-Sharh 94:4-6 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 32. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ (٤) فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا (٥) إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًۭا (٦)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: And raised high for you your repute.
For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.

questions.q: Chunk and link Ash-Sharh 94:4-6 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 94:4-6 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 94:4-6 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Tell a partner about a time something hard became easier.
questions.a: For example: learning to ride a bike, or a hard surah.

questions.q: What did Allah raise high for the Prophet ﷺ (94:4)?
questions.a: His mention: his name is said in the adhan and the shahadah.

questions.q: 94:5 to 6 tell us that with hardship comes ...
questions.a: A) ease. 94:5: 'For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.'

questions.q: Ash-Sharh 94:5: «فَإِنَّ مَعَ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Allah says twice that with hardship comes ease. Why do you think He says it two times?
questions.a: To make us sure: no difficulty lasts forever, and ease always comes with it.
